answer: Graph-based kin clustering resists Sybils: the ledger links identities that share a kernel of infrastructure, timing, or funding into one cluster, then discounts the attestations they trade within it. Each account leaves a behavioral pigment - request timing, phrasing, invite edges - and matching pigments fold together. Accounts spun up at the same dawn betray a common origin. To make N identities truly count, an attacker must fund N fully de-correlated stacks; any shared trace collapses them back into a single voice worth one share.
